question: Does the official BFAR CALABARZON 2020 report expose fish taxa or locate its Rapid Resource Assessments well enough to add coastal fish records?

source.title: BFAR CALABARZON Annual Report 2020
findings: The report says 11 fish-sanctuary sites were assisted through Rapid Resource Assessment (RRA).
Table 8 names Ternate / Senemento Reef and Maragondon / Patungan Reef among the 2020 monitored or assessed sites.
The preceding assistance table separately lists Ternate / monitoring of an artificial reef; the report does not say whether this was the same activity or station as the RRA entry.

crossChecks.title: State of the Coasts of Cavite Province
crossChecks.locator: Printed page 82, Table 18; PDF text lines 3004-3010
crossChecks.finding: Lists Ternate Ordinance No. 04 S-2005 and Resolution No. 17 S-2005 declaring Bulaklakin Reef a fish sanctuary and fishery reserve. This is historical governance context, not a current legal-status verification or fish survey.

crossChecks.title: GEF Small Grants Programme project page: Conservation and Protection of Bulaklakin Reef Fish Sanctuary
crossChecks.access: Indexed page excerpt reviewed; direct page open returned 403
crossChecks.finding: The indexed project description says an April 2005 rapid risk assessment found live corals and fishes over 37-40% of reef area, and that a survey was conducted through BFAR in 2008. It supplies no fish taxa or station-level results in the excerpt. These are retrieval leads, not fish records.

crossChecks.title: Cavite Ecological Profile 2023
crossChecks.locator: Map 2.11 Coral Reef Locator Map, Province of Cavite: 2022
crossChecks.finding: The BFAR IV-A-sourced map labels a Maragondon Patungan reef marker and uses the spelling Sementeno for the Ternate marker. This is map-name context only; it does not establish a station or boundary crosswalk.

limitations: The BFAR annual report provides no fish taxa, species counts, survey dates at the site level, RRA protocol, observer names, coordinates, or voucher/identification support.
Senemento/Sementeno spelling variation requires name resolution; do not merge those labels with other reefs from spelling alone.
Patungan Reef in Maragondon is not assumed to be the same feature as Sitio Patungan Munti or the candidate Limbones Cove reef lead.
The Bulaklakin Reef 2005/2008 statements do not establish current habitat condition, current fish presence, catchability, safety, or applicable present-day fishing rules.
No report-specific public reuse license was verified for the annual report or underlying assessment tables.
nextAction: Locate the underlying 2020 RRA records for Ternate Senemento Reef and Maragondon Patungan Reef, plus the cited 2005/2008 Bulaklakin Reef assessments. Confirm site-name and station crosswalks, dates, methods, taxon rank, identification/voucher support and item-specific reuse terms. Do not merge Patungan Reef with Patungan Munti or transfer any of these coastal records to Maragondon River/Estuary.
